clue.text: Risky game in which players keep their eyes on the ball

definitions.text: Risky game in which players keep their eyes on the ball

parts.words: Risky game in which players keep their eyes on the ball
parts.note: a casino gamble where everyone watches a small ball spin round a wheel, not a sports match

explanation.surface: Players in some dangerous sport watch the ball closely.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ball game such as cricket; the ball is the little one dropped on a spinning casino wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling wheel game where bettors stake money on where a small ball lands.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A dispatch says certain troops are running behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to recount or tell it.

parts.note: a foreman is the senior worker, the superior labourer, so has the dominant position

explanation.surface: What benefit comes from supervising a workforce?
explanation.walkthrough: A hand is a worker, so a foreman is a higher-placed one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a position of control or dominance.

clue.text: One kind of crop, we hear is consumed

indicators.note: tells us the word is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: an Eton crop is a short 1920s hairstyle named after the school

explanation.surface: A certain harvest, rumour has it, is used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' suggests farming; the Eton crop is a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is eaten has been consumed.

clue.text: Reprimand means that no further credit will be given

definitions.text: no further credit will be given
definitions.meaning: tick is British slang for credit, so the tick is off

explanation.surface: A rebuke implies the account is closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or tell someone off sharply.

definitions.meaning: forms are classes of pupils, and a whole teaching establishment holds several of them
a shoal of fish swimming together goes by the same collective noun

explanation.surface: Certain shapes of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaching establishment is made up of forms, and a shoal of fish has the same collective name.

parts.note: both are cities that gave their names to kinds of porcelain, so each is a porcelain city

explanation.surface: Two cities, one German and one Chinese, offered as examples.
explanation.walkthrough: Dresden and Nanking are both types of porcelain, which is called china.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese district in a Western city; read literally, a city famed for porcelain.

parts.note: in tennis a ball landing beyond the line is out
to do is to serve, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: A wayward tennis serve costs the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass or beat someone.

parts.note: a pride is a group of big cats, and their lair is the home

explanation.surface: A house one can feel proud of.
explanation.walkthrough: Pride is the collective noun for big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: The lair of a group of big cats; also any dangerous place.

parts.note: Cupid's bow is the curved shape of the upper lip, and the drawer is the cosmetic that outlines it

explanation.surface: Who pulls back the bow of the god of love?
explanation.walkthrough: Drawer looks like an archer drawing a bow, but it means something that draws a line; Cupid's bow is the curve of the upper lip.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic stick used to colour and outline the mouth, including the curve called Cupid's bow.

clue.text: Way out writer in French restaurant

indicators.note: here the writer stands out, on the outside, with the way enclosed within it

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen, a writer
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: An eccentric author dines at a Parisian eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way out' reads as eccentric, yet the two words split: 'out' signals the writer standing outside. A biro is a British ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, informal eating place of the kind associated with France.

parts.note: credit is the opposite of what is owed, in accounting terms, not belief

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Credit' reads as believe; in accounts a sum owed sits on the opposite side.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owed, the opposite of a credit in bookkeeping.

clue.text: Modern city can be built round ancient one

indicators.note: the can is constructed so that it surrounds the old city

parts.note: a tin is a can
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, the one referring back to city

explanation.surface: A present-day town can be erected over the ruins of an old one.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial city of present-day northern Italy, capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: They work for exceptionally poor rates

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an unusual, out-of-the-ordinary way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some people labour for very low pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Operators are people who run machines or handle switchboards, that is, who work.

clue.text: Wages get stopped as the final part of a joke

definitions.text: the final part of a joke

parts.note: pay is wages
something called off is stopped

explanation.surface: Workers' pay is halted, which is the punchline of some cruel joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The punchline that resolves a joke is its climax or pay-off line.

clue.text: Away from work for the rest of the year

definitions.text: Away from work for the rest of the year

parts.words: Away from work for the rest of the year
parts.note: the rest is a break, a vacation taken during the year, not the remaining months

explanation.surface: Someone has stopped working until next January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The rest of the year' suggests the remaining months; it is a rest taken in the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a vacation means being away from work for a spell.

parts.note: from the saying two's company, three's a crowd
an occasion is a time

explanation.surface: Asks whether a firm cheats now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' looks like a firm; it is the number in 'two's company, three's a crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unfaithful to a partner by secretly seeing someone else, a form of deceit.

clue.text: Put in for one stripe during manoeuvres

indicators.note: the letters are moved about as troops are in exercises

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier with one stripe is put forward during military exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to insert or place something between.

parts.note: literally held in the arms lovingly, rather than regarded fondly

explanation.surface: Someone is much loved.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests being esteemed; here it is literal holding in a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugged warmly, clasped in someone's arms.

clue.text: Openly took advantage of the sunshine?

definitions.text: Openly took advantage of the sunshine?

parts.words: Openly took advantage of the sunshine?
parts.note: the proverb about turning grass into dry fodder while the sun shines, read literally of a farmer working in the open

explanation.surface: Someone exploited the fine weather in full view.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says to do this while the sun shines; it means seizing an opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have exploited an opportunity, from farmers drying grass in sunny weather.

indicators.note: the name sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man from France wears a dirty singlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A common French masculine name.

clue.text: Excellent to include it, within limits

indicators.note: the word for excellent is made to take in the next piece

parts.note: fine means excellent

explanation.surface: It is splendid to include it, as long as it stays moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bounded or limited in extent rather than endless.

parts.note: inferior in its sense of lower down: hair growing low on a horse's leg

explanation.surface: Some poor-quality horsehair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inferior' means low down on the leg, not poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint above a horse's hoof and the tuft of hair growing behind it.

definitions.meaning: persisted, as in lasting the distance
did not go, remained in place

explanation.surface: Someone carried on, or perhaps not.
explanation.definitionFit: Persisted in a race; equally, remained rather than leaving.

parts.note: to repel is to drive away
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: It's disgusting, so chase it off quickly!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as quickly, but it is the noun: LENT is the Christian season of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Repellent describes something disgusting that makes one recoil.

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A committee on prison reform.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a board of people, as of judges or experts.

clue.text: Go to pieces, because of over-inflation?

definitions.text: Go to pieces, because of over-inflation?

parts.words: Go to pieces, because of over-inflation?
parts.note: a balloon or tyre pumped up too far shatters, rather than an economy overheating

explanation.surface: An economy collapses through runaway price rises.
explanation.walkthrough: Over-inflation suggests economics; here it is too much air in a balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: To break apart suddenly, as a balloon does when given too much air.

parts.note: not a company but the largest land animal of the continent, which supplies meat

explanation.surface: The leading meat-packing firm in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a business; it is the largest land mammal of North America.
explanation.definitionFit: The American buffalo, the heaviest land animal in North America.

indicators.note: in an across answer the girl's name is placed on, that is after, the vessel

parts.note: a can is a vessel
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman from the countryside is aboard the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country girl' reads as one phrase, but 'Country' is the definition and 'girl' is ADA.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American nation, the second largest in the world by area.

parts.note: a hound's corpse is what lies buried in an animal graveyard, but the phrase is also slang for a drudge

explanation.surface: A labourer works in an animal graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a drudge who does the menial jobs is so called; the cemetery points to a dead hound.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a drudge who does menial work for others.

definitions.meaning: hold-ups such as traffic jams make you late
a verb here: puts off or postpones

explanation.surface: These things support shelving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelves' reads as a noun; as a verb it means postpones.
explanation.definitionFit: Hold-ups are hindrances, and shelving a plan means putting it off.

clue.text: Bitter about relative, he becomes a young thug

indicators.note: the word for bitter goes round the other pieces

parts.note: sad can mean bitter, as in a sad or bitter experience
kin are relatives
taken as written

explanation.surface: Resentful towards a family member, a man turns into a youthful hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaven-headed youth, often linked with violent street gangs.
